terms.plainEnglish: A fast frontend dev server and build tool.
terms.beginnerExplanation: Vite is the tool that helps run and build many modern frontend apps.
terms.learningExplanation: Vite provides a fast dev server, hot module replacement, and production builds.
terms.advancedExplanation: Vite uses native ESM during development and Rollup-powered production builds.
terms.confusion: Vite is not React itself. It is the tool that runs and builds the app.

terms.plainEnglish: Usually starts Vite's local development server so you can preview the app while editing.
terms.beginnerExplanation: npm run dev usually starts the app on your computer while you work.
terms.learningExplanation: npm run dev runs the dev script from package.json, often starting Vite's dev server.
terms.advancedExplanation: npm run dev invokes the configured development script, commonly vite in watch/dev-server mode.
terms.confusion: This server is for development. It is not the final production build.

terms.plainEnglish: Usually asks Vite to create optimized files for deployment.
terms.beginnerExplanation: npm run build creates the files you would put online for users.
terms.learningExplanation: npm run build runs the build script, usually producing optimized static output.
terms.advancedExplanation: npm run build invokes the production bundling pipeline.
terms.confusion: Build output is normally written to a folder like dist and is separate from your source files.

terms.plainEnglish: A name for your own computer when a dev server runs locally.
terms.beginnerExplanation: localhost means the app is running on your own computer.
terms.learningExplanation: localhost points to your machine, often with a port like localhost:5173.
terms.advancedExplanation: localhost resolves to loopback networking for services running on the local machine.
terms.confusion: Other people cannot normally visit your localhost address from their computer.

terms.plainEnglish: A development feature that updates the browser quickly after you save changes.
terms.beginnerExplanation: Hot reload updates the page after you save without starting over manually.
terms.learningExplanation: Hot reload or HMR updates changed modules in the browser during development.
terms.advancedExplanation: Hot module replacement swaps changed modules while preserving app state when possible.
terms.confusion: Hot reload is a dev convenience. It is not something users rely on in production.
terms.example: Save App.jsx and the browser updates.
